candidates.title: ❌ You're Doing Dumbbell Shrugs WRONG!
candidates.description:
❌ You're Doing Dumbbell Shrugs WRONG!

Mistake #1: Hunching Your Back
This puts stress on your spine and increases the risk of injury. Instead, keep a neutral back with your chest tall and core braced.

Mistake #2: Holding the Dumbbells at Your Sides
When the dumbbells are directly beside you, they can rub against your thighs, making the movement awkward and less effective.. Try positioning them slightly in front of your body.

Mistake #3: Staying Fully Upright
Staying completely vertical limits trap engagement. Leaning forward slightly hits more of the upper and middle traps—and often feels more natural on your shoulders.

Mistake #4: Rolling Your Shoulders
Rolling adds unnecessary joint stress and does nothing for muscle activation. Shrug straight up and down with control.

candidates.title: How to PROPERLY Dumbbell Shrug (FIX THIS NOW!)
candidates.description:
➢ Message me "Free Guide" to IG @ColossusFit to get your free personal trainer in your pocket

Want to grow bigger traps and master dumbbell shrugs? In this video, I break down the best tips for dumbbell shrugs and the most common mistakes to avoid so you can build muscle safely and effectively.

Dumbbell shrugs are one of the best exercises for trap development, but most people do them wrong. If you’ve been rolling your shoulders, using too much weight, or cutting your range of motion short, you’re leaving gains on the table (and putting your joints at risk).

Here’s what we cover:

✅ Dumbbell Shrug Mistakes to Avoid:
- Rolling the shoulders — Shrugs are straight up and down, not circles. Rolling only adds stress, not size.
- Using momentum/too much weight — Jerking or bouncing prevents full trap activation.
- Short range of motion — Half-repping shrugs means missing out on real growth.

✅ Dumbbell Shrug Tips for Better Form:

- Stand tall: chest up, core braced.
- Arms straight: dumbbells hang naturally, no bent elbows.
- Up to your ears: imagine touching shoulders to ears for max contraction.
- Straight up, straight down: no rolling, no leaning forward.
- Squeeze at the top: 1–2 second hold for full trap engagement.
- Controlled lowering: don’t drop the weights — control every rep.

Whether you’re training traps for bodybuilding, strength, or aesthetics, this guide will help you do dumbbell shrugs correctly and avoid the mistakes that hold most lifters back.

🔥 Perfect for beginners learning proper shrug technique, or experienced lifters who want to fix their form and get more out of trap training.

candidates.title: Dumbbell Shrug - Traps Exercise
candidates.description:
Dumbbell Shrug - Traps Exercise

Download the app: https://mytraining.pro/

Read our community blog: http://friends.mytraining.pro/

(Starting Position)

Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your sides and your arms extended close to your body.

Keep your back straight, your torso slightly bent forward, and your shoulder blades pinned back. This is the starting position. 

(First movement) 

Now, exhale as you use your traps to raise the weights while shrugging your shoulders up and as far back as possible. Tightly contract your traps at the end of the movement.

(Second Movement)

Inhale as you slowly lower the weights back to the starting position.

(General Advice)

Only your shoulders should move during this exercise, so be sure to keep your arms extended.
